solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bread for former US magazine personnel?

definitions.meaning: bread is called the basic support of life in the old phrase from the Bible
the people who worked on Life, the American picture magazine that stopped weekly publication in 1972

explanation.surface: A question about what the old employees of an American magazine were paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' looks like slang for wages paid to the staff; it is the food itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase calls bread the basic food that keeps people alive, as in the old proverb.

parts.note: a striptease that shocks its audience leaves very little clothing on, so the clue hints at a lack or thinness of covering

explanation.surface: A stripper's skimpy outfit is causing outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: The striptease picture points to a shortage of clothes; the answer is the general word for having very little of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarcity or thinness of something is the meaning of the word, so it works as a synonym for scantiness.

clue.text: As stroll develops, a mixture of sweets is required

indicators.note: as something develops it changes shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone taking a walk picks up a bag of mixed sweets along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'develops' rearranges the letters of AS STROLL.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquorice Allsorts are a well-known British assortment of mixed liquorice sweets, and the word is also used for any mixture.

clue.text: Conifers on top of tor, higher than the others

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on top of another comes before it

parts.note: firs are conifers, cone-bearing evergreen trees

indicators.note: the top of a word in this clue means its opening letter, as a hill's top is its summit

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill; only its opening letter is used here

explanation.surface: Pine trees growing on a high rocky hill stand above the rest of the landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky hilltop, common on Dartmoor in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Being the one ranked above all the others means being placed at the front, a synonym.

clue.text: Absent-minded physicist's day turns into week

indicators.note: one thing turning into another means a letter is swapped for a different one

parts.note: Michael Faraday was the English physicist who studied electricity

explanation.surface: A scientist so distracted that he loses track of time and a day becomes a week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns into' replaces the D in FARADAY with W.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamy, distant look describes someone whose mind is elsewhere, a synonym.

parts.note: to deduce is to infer, reaching a conclusion from evidence
NO is a common abbreviation for the US city New Orleans

explanation.surface: Someone concludes that a hot and sticky American city is hell on earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante's word for the underworld of torment is a standard synonym for hell.

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition is just the poet

parts.note: Ezra is a book of the Old Testament
before decimal currency came in 1971, a British pound was made up of twenty shillings

explanation.surface: A poet's book is priced at twenty shillings back in 1970.
explanation.walkthrough: Britain changed to decimal money in 1971, so in 1970 twenty shillings still made one pound.
explanation.definitionFit: The American modernist author of the Cantos is the poet named here, an example of the class.

definitions.meaning: in cricket the ... side of the field is also called the on side
an arm or ... is a limb

explanation.surface: A three-word phrase saying someone is out on a limb.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the half of the field behind a right-handed batsman's legs is the leg side, also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the lower limbs, and a cricket term for the on side, are the two meanings.

parts.note: a net is a snare for catching animals

explanation.surface: A bird has been abandoned in a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A small finch found across Britain is the bird, an example of the class.

clue.text: Grand facility across river for oil

indicators.note: one piece lying across another spans it, holding it inside

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
facility and ease both mean doing something without difficulty

explanation.surface: A big industrial plant on a river is used to store oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' puts R inside GEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: To lubricate machinery with fat or oil is the verb sense, a synonym.

clue.text: US musician playing lead guitar at the end

indicators.note: playing about with letters rearranges them
the piece at the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: An American musician plays lead guitar at the close of a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges LEAD to ADLE. Larry Adler was the American harmonica virtuoso, not a guitarist.
explanation.definitionFit: Larry Adler was a celebrated American harmonica player, so the surname names a US musician.

indicators.note: a chess player sacrificing a piece gives it up, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a favourite is someone's preference
P is the chess abbreviation for pawn

explanation.surface: A chess commentary mentions a player's favourite pawn sacrifice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacrificing' removes P from PREFERENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A passing allusion to something is a synonym for a mention of it.

clue.text: Two others injured where ammunition was made

indicators.note: something injured is knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two more people are hurt in an explosion at a munitions works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two others' sounds like more casualties, but 'injured' is the anagram signal. In a shot tower, molten lead fell from the top and cooled into round balls of shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall tower was used to make lead shot by dropping molten metal, so it describes such a factory.

definitions.meaning: to iron clothes is to smooth them flat
a cupboard with shelves, especially in Scotland or for linen

explanation.surface: An iron is kept in the cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to smooth clothes flat and a shelved cupboard, so it serves both senses.

parts.note: taken as written
two accounts that match tally with each other

explanation.surface: A phrase about things matching completely.
explanation.definitionFit: Completely and wholly mean the same as in every respect, a synonym.

clue.text: New title includes second Kipling poem with a recurring theme

indicators.note: one piece including another holds it inside
a new version of the word is made by rearranging its letters

parts.note: MO is short for moment, a second
If is a famous poem by Rudyard Kipling

explanation.surface: A fresh heading is added to a Kipling poem that keeps coming back to one idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges the clue's fodder to LEITT, and 'includes' puts the abbreviation for a second inside it, just before the closing letters; the poem is added last.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical or literary idea that keeps returning through a work is a synonym of the German-derived term.

indicators.note: a word losing its heading loses its first letter

parts.note: a tip given for good service is a bonus

explanation.surface: A heavy load is carried away from a rubbish tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' looks like a rubbish dump; it is a gratuity, and 'heading off' drops the first letter of BONUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden or responsibility placed on someone is a figurative synonym for load.

parts.note: to get on in life is to prosper

explanation.surface: A man gets along with an elderly aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: Prospero is the rightful Duke of Milan in Shakespeare's play The Tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's magician in The Tempest is the deposed Duke of Milan, an example.

clue.text: Beast could make social worker run away

parts.note: an ant is a worker in a social insect colony
to elope is to run away secretly to marry

explanation.surface: A wild animal could cause a social worker to flee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' suggests a welfare officer; it is an insect from a social colony.
explanation.definitionFit: A swift horned African grazing animal is an example of a beast.

clue.text: Record American lost in field event

indicators.note: a part lost in a word disappears from it, so it is removed

parts.note: the discus is a field event in athletics

explanation.surface: An American's record throw is lost at an athletics event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost in' removes US from DISCUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A gramophone record is a flat round disc, a synonym.

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check
amber is a yellowish-orange colour

explanation.surface: An inspector checks the paint colour used in a room.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned word for a room, especially a bedroom, a synonym.

parts.note: sad can mean shabby or pitifully poor in quality
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A scruffy golf club is used one evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evening' is not the time of day but making things even, as a flat iron smooths cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: An old heavy flat iron heated on a stove was used for smoothing clothes, that is, making them even.

clue.text: Cheers wildly after drinking Canadian's capital dark rum

indicators.note: a piece drinking another takes it inside
letters behaving wildly are thrown into a new order
a word's capital is its initial letter

explanation.surface: Revellers cheer wildly after drinking dark rum from Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' rearranges CHEERS to SREECH, and 'after drinking' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Screech is a strong dark rum from Newfoundland in Canada, so it is a name for that drink.

definitions.meaning: an aim is a goal or purpose
to protest is to raise an objection

explanation.surface: A protester sets out their purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a goal and to raise objection, so it serves both senses.

indicators.note: something odd is out of the normal order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark on the strange character of a Russian tea vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' rearranges NATURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A samovar is a Russian urn for heating water for tea, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Fish, ray, round mouth of river

indicators.note: one piece round another surrounds it, holding it inside

parts.note: a beam is a ray of light

indicators.note: the mouth of a word is its first letter, as a river begins at its mouth in this clue

explanation.surface: A fish and a ray swim around the mouth of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ray' looks like another fish; it is a beam of light.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater carp-family fish is an example of a fish.

indicators.note: something perplexed is tangled or mixed up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ambitious person makes an infrequent, puzzled visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perplexed' rearranges RARE VISIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A French-derived word for an ambitious person trying to rise in society, a synonym.

clue.text: Doodlebug landed on vehicle of clergyman

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece landing on another sits above it

parts.note: the doodlebug was the V1 flying bomb used by Germany in the Second World War, read as V and I
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A flying bomb crashed onto a priest's car.
explanation.walkthrough: Doodlebug was the British wartime nickname for the German V1 flying bomb; the 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish priest in the Church of England is an example of a clergyman.

indicators.note: one piece about another goes round it

parts.note: an even-tempered person is equable

explanation.surface: A calm-natured person from Italy is fair-minded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even-tempered' looks like the definition of the answer, but it is the outer piece; 'fair' at the end is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and impartial treatment is a synonym for fair.

clue.text: Set of beliefs about inner circle

parts.note: C is short for circa, about
the inner ring of a dartboard's bull is red
a circle is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A creed held by a group's privileged inner circle.
explanation.walkthrough: On a dartboard the inner bull is red, so 'inner' gives RED.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement of faith or guiding principles is a synonym for a set of beliefs.

parts.note: an means one, as in 'an apple'

explanation.surface: A musician keeps the beat with a single tap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat' looks like a musical pulse; it is the verb to thrash.
explanation.definitionFit: To tan someone's hide is an informal idiom for beating them.

clue.text: Public indignation about the Royal Mail as well

indicators.note: one piece about another surrounds it

parts.note: a furore is an outbreak of public anger
taken as written
RM is the abbreviation for Royal Mail, the British postal service

explanation.surface: There is public outrage over the postal service as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Public indignation' looks like the start of a news story; 'about' wraps that outrage round the inner pieces. Royal Mail is Britain's national postal service.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides and in addition both mean the same as as well, a synonym.
